projectFiles.title: Akai · Project file and project-data loading

definitions.title: MIDI is not the sound
definitions.text: MIDI communicates performance and control information. An instrument interprets it and produces audio. Keeping the note instructions is different from recording that instrument's actual sound.

definitions.title: A meter is one checkpoint
definitions.text: A meter shows activity at its own location. It does not prove that every later destination receives that signal. In AUM, the input, effects, and output are distinct nodes; identify which point you are measuring.

definitions.title: Data and power are separate questions
definitions.text: USB data role describes the connection's role; power role describes charging. Akai directs smartphone connections toward Act as Device on the G2. That setting alone does not prove the cable, app routing, or power behavior is stable.

definitions.title: Hearing is not capturing
definitions.text: Choose what you need to keep: performance instructions, the audio result, or supported control changes. Our test is to inspect what was recorded and replay it deliberately—not infer success from live monitoring.

definitions.title: A project has dependencies
definitions.text: The visible project file and its associated data belong together. Careless moves or renames can break loading. Our practical check is to save, locate, reopen, and compare against a recognizable result.

definitions.title: What exactly am I changing?
definitions.text: Always identify the selected object and the control's place in the path. Lowering one channel is a different intention from lowering the listening output. Predict which sounds should change, then listen for the result.

techniques.title: Change a phrase into an instrument
techniques.text: Separate capture, selection, assignment, and performance. The question is not merely whether a waveform was recorded, but how your hands can use it.
techniques.experiment: After sampling fundamentals: choose one of your own sounds and make two contrasting articulations. Exact MPC playback controls must be verified on the installed OS.

techniques.title: Preserve instructions and result separately
techniques.text: A MIDI performance can remain editable while an audio recording preserves the external instrument's actual sound. The two records answer different needs.
techniques.experiment: With a stable external route: compare a short MIDI performance and an audio capture. Identify which changes remain editable and which are printed.

techniques.title: Bound a live control
techniques.text: The G2 troubleshooting guide discusses Q-Link macro learning and momentary behavior. Availability and the exact target must be checked before relying on a mapping.
techniques.experiment: After basic controls: map one available target, establish a comfortable range, test its return, then test automation capture separately.

techniques.title: Reuse a proven phone route
techniques.text: AUM can save sessions and import channels from another session. Reusing a proven path is different from rebuilding the same setup each time.
techniques.experiment: Only after the phone route works: save a named AUM session, reopen it, and test the route again. Record any hardware-dependent choices that must be restored.

note: This initial reference is deliberately small. The earlier Technique Map retains the broader research list while sources and version-specific instructions are checked for each new lesson. No feature is marked practiced merely because it is documented.
